jp: 母[はは]の作[つく]る料理[りょうり]は、いつも味[あじ]が{濃[こ]い|cl-adj}です。
en: The food my mother makes always has a strong, heavily seasoned flavor.
why: Flavor that is strongly seasoned is 味が濃い; 濃い/薄い is the pair for taste.

jp: 病院[びょういん]の食事[しょくじ]は味[あじ]が{薄[うす]くて|cl-adj}、あまり好[す]きではありません。
en: Hospital meals are weakly seasoned and I don't like them much.
why: Bland, lightly seasoned taste is 味が薄い; 濃い/薄い describes flavor.

jp: このお茶[ちゃ]は{薄[うす]すぎる|cl-adj}ので、入[い]れ直[なお]してください。
en: This tea is too weak, so please make it again.
why: Tea is thick or thin in strength: 濃いお茶 / 薄いお茶, so weak tea is 薄い.

jp: 眠[ねむ]くならないように、{濃[こ]い|cl-adj}お茶[ちゃ]を飲[の]みました。
en: To keep from getting sleepy, I drank strong tea.
why: Strong, concentrated tea is 濃いお茶; the pair 濃い/薄い is used for drinks.

jp: 今日[きょう]は{濃[こ]い|cl-adj}青[あお]のシャツを着[き]ています。
en: Today I'm wearing a dark blue shirt.
why: A deep, saturated color is 濃い (濃い青 = dark blue); pale is 薄い.

jp: 壁[かべ]の色[いろ]は{薄[うす]い|cl-adj}ピンクがいいと思[おも]います。
en: I think a pale pink would be good for the wall color.
why: A pale color is 薄い (薄いピンク); 軽い is not used for colors in Japanese.

jp: 今日[きょう]は風[かぜ]が{強[つよ]い|cl-adj}ので、自転車[じてんしゃ]に乗[の]るのは大変[たいへん]です。
en: The wind is strong today, so riding a bicycle is hard.
why: Wind is strong or weak: 風が強い / 風が弱い.

jp: 台風[たいふう]が近[ちか]づいて、夜[よる]から風[かぜ]が{強[つよ]く|cl-adj}なりました。
en: As the typhoon approached, the wind grew strong from nightfall.
why: The wind's force is 強い; 風が強くなる means the wind picks up.

jp: 窓[まど]から{弱[よわ]い|cl-adj}風[かぜ]が入[はい]ってきて、気持[きも]ちがよかったです。
en: A gentle breeze came in through the window and it felt good.
why: A weak, gentle wind is 弱い風; the pair for wind is 強い/弱い.

jp: 田中[たなか]さんはお酒[さけ]が{強[つよ]い|cl-adj}ので、いくら飲[の]んでも酔[よ]いません。
en: Mr. Tanaka can hold his liquor, so he doesn't get drunk however much he drinks.
why: Being a good drinker is お酒が強い; 強い/弱い is the pair for alcohol tolerance.

jp: 私[わたし]はお酒[さけ]が{弱[よわ]い|cl-adj}ので、ビールを一杯[いっぱい]飲[の]むと顔[かお]が赤[あか]くなります。
en: I can't hold my liquor, so my face turns red after one glass of beer.
why: Low alcohol tolerance is お酒が弱い; it is the opposite of お酒が強い.

jp: 午後[ごご]から風[かぜ]が{弱[よわ]く|cl-adj}なるそうです。
en: I hear the wind will weaken from the afternoon.
why: When the wind dies down, 風が弱くなる is the set phrase; 強い/弱い pairs with wind.

jp: 祖父[そふ]は{重[おも]い|cl-adj}病気[びょうき]で、三[さん]か月[げつ]入院[にゅういん]しています。
en: My grandfather has a serious illness and has been in hospital for three months.
why: A serious illness is 重い病気; 重い/軽い is the pair for how grave an illness is.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]は{軽[かる]い|cl-adj}病気[びょうき]ですが、休[やす]むことが大切[たいせつ]です。
en: A cold is a minor illness, but resting is important.
why: A mild illness is 軽い病気, the opposite of 重い病気.

jp: 社長[しゃちょう]になると、責任[せきにん]が{重[おも]く|cl-adj}なります。
en: When you become company president, your responsibility becomes heavy.
why: Responsibility is heavy: 責任が重い; 重い/軽い pairs with 責任.

jp: 新人[しんじん]のうちは、責任[せきにん]の{軽[かる]い|cl-adj}仕事[しごと]から始[はじ]めます。
en: While you are new, you start with jobs that carry little responsibility.
why: Little responsibility is 責任が軽い, the opposite of 責任が重い.

jp: 子[こ]どもの熱[ねつ]が{高[たか]い|cl-adj}ので、病院[びょういん]へ連[つ]れて行[い]きました。
en: My child's fever was high, so I took them to the hospital.
why: A fever is high or low: 熱が高い / 熱が低い.

jp: 朝[あさ]は熱[ねつ]が{低[ひく]かった|cl-adj}のに、夜[よる]になってまた上[あ]がりました。
en: My fever was low in the morning, but it went up again at night.
why: A fever is high or low, so a mild temperature is 熱が低い; 高い/低い is the pair for temperature.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は{高[たか]い|cl-adj}声[こえ]で歌[うた]います。
en: My younger sister sings in a high voice.
why: A high-pitched voice is 高い声; 高い/低い pairs with 声.

jp: あの俳優[はいゆう]は{低[ひく]い|cl-adj}声[こえ]で話[はな]すので、とても落[お]ち着[つ]いて見[み]えます。
en: That actor speaks in a low voice, so he looks very calm.
why: A deep, low-pitched voice is 低い声, the opposite of 高い声.

jp: 夜[よる]になって、雨[あめ]が{激[はげ]しく|cl-adj}降[ふ]り始[はじ]めました。
en: When night came, the rain began to fall hard.
why: Violent, heavy rain is 雨が激しい; 激しく降る is the fixed way to say it pours.

jp: 医者[いしゃ]に、{激[はげ]しい|cl-adj}運動[うんどう]は当分[とうぶん]しないように言[い]われました。
en: The doctor told me not to do intense exercise for the time being.
why: Hard, intense exercise is 激しい運動; none of the other options collocates with 運動.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]が止[と]まるほどの{激[はげ]しい|cl-adj}雨[あめ]でした。
en: It was such violent rain that the trains stopped.
why: Torrential rain is 激しい雨; 濃い or 重い cannot describe rain.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]の荷物[にもつ]が{重[おも]くて|cl-adj}、階段[かいだん]を上[のぼ]るのが大変[たいへん]でした。
en: My luggage for the trip was heavy, so climbing the stairs was hard.
why: Physical weight is 重い; luggage is heavy or light, 重い/軽い.

jp: コーヒーは{濃[こ]い|cl-adj}のと薄[うす]いの、どちらが好[す]きですか。
en: Which do you like, strong coffee or weak coffee?
why: Strong versus weak coffee is 濃い versus 薄い, the pair for the strength of drinks.

jp: 健康[けんこう]のために、{薄[うす]い|cl-adj}味[あじ]の料理[りょうり]を作[つく]っています。
en: For my health, I cook lightly seasoned food.
why: Lightly seasoned flavor is 薄い味; the opposite is 濃い味.

jp: 朝[あさ]は{濃[こ]い|cl-adj}霧[きり]が出[で]て、前[まえ]がよく見[み]えませんでした。
en: A thick fog came in the morning and I couldn't see ahead well.
why: Dense fog is 濃い霧; 濃い/薄い describes density as well as taste and color.

jp: このコーヒーは{薄[うす]くて|cl-adj}、水[みず]みたいです。
en: This coffee is weak; it's like water.
why: Coffee that lacks strength is 薄い, the opposite of 濃い.

jp: 大[おお]きな会社[かいしゃ]を守[まも]るのは、{重[おも]い|cl-adj}責任[せきにん]です。
en: Looking after a big company is a heavy responsibility.
why: Responsibility is heavy: 重い責任 is the fixed collocation.

jp: 仕事[しごと]を変[か]えたら、責任[せきにん]が{軽[かる]く|cl-adj}なって、気持[きも]ちが楽[らく]になりました。
en: After I changed jobs, my responsibilities became lighter and I felt more at ease.
why: Lighter duties are 責任が軽くなる; the opposite is 責任が重くなる.

jp: 今日[きょう]は風[かぜ]が{強[つよ]い|cl-adj}ですね。傘[かさ]が飛[と]ばされそうです。
en: It's windy today, isn't it? My umbrella looks like it will blow away.
why: Wind that can blow an umbrella away is 風が強い.

jp: 熱[ねつ]が{高[たか]かった|cl-adj}ので、昨日[きのう]は一日[いちにち]寝[ね]ていました。
en: I had a high fever, so I stayed in bed all day yesterday.
why: A fever is measured as high or low, so 熱が高い.

jp: 熱[ねつ]はあまり{高[たか]く|cl-adj}ありませんから、心配[しんぱい]しないでください。
en: The fever isn't very high, so please don't worry.
why: 熱が高い is the natural phrase, and the negative form is 高くありません.

jp: 電話[でんわ]の声[こえ]が{低[ひく]くて|cl-adj}、男[おとこ]の人[ひと]かと思[おも]いました。
en: The voice on the phone was low, so I thought it was a man.
why: A voice of low pitch is 声が低い; 低い/高い is the pair for pitch.

jp: 子[こ]どもの{高[たか]い|cl-adj}声[こえ]が公園[こうえん]から聞[き]こえます。
en: I can hear the children's high voices from the park.
why: High-pitched voices are 高い声; none of the other adjectives goes with 声.

jp: 病気[びょうき]が{重[おも]い|cl-adj}ので、今[いま]は誰[だれ]にも会[あ]えません。
en: The illness is serious, so nobody can see them at the moment.
why: A grave illness is 病気が重い; 重い/軽い measures the seriousness of an illness.

jp: 医者[いしゃ]の話[はなし]では、{軽[かる]い|cl-adj}病気[びょうき]なのですぐ治[なお]るそうです。
en: According to the doctor it is a mild illness, so it should clear up soon.
why: A mild illness that heals quickly is 軽い病気, the opposite of 重い病気.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]{激[はげ]しい|cl-adj}運動[うんどう]を続[つづ]けたので、足[あし]が痛[いた]くなりました。
en: I kept doing intense exercise every day, so my legs began to hurt.
why: Strenuous exercise is 激しい運動; 激しい also describes heavy rain.

jp: 窓[まど]の外[そと]では、雨[あめ]が{激[はげ]しく|cl-adj}降[ふ]っています。
en: Outside the window the rain is falling hard.
why: Rain pouring violently is 雨が激しく降る; the other adjectives do not fit rain.

jp: 父[ちち]は{強[つよ]い|cl-adj}お酒[さけ]が好[す]きで、ウイスキーをよく飲[の]みます。
en: My father likes strong liquor and often drinks whiskey.
why: High-proof drink is 強いお酒; 強い/弱い is the pair for alcohol.

jp: 洗濯[せんたく]したら、シャツの色[いろ]が{薄[うす]く|cl-adj}なってしまいました。
en: After I washed it, the color of the shirt faded.
why: A color that has faded is 色が薄くなる; the opposite is 色が濃くなる.

jp: この赤[あか]は色[いろ]が{濃[こ]すぎて|cl-adj}、私[わたし]には派手[はで]です。
en: This red is too deep a color, so it's too flashy for me.
why: A color that is too saturated is 色が濃い, so 濃すぎて fits.

jp: 部長[ぶちょう]に、{重[おも]い|cl-adj}責任[せきにん]を任[まか]されました。
en: The department head entrusted me with a heavy responsibility.
why: Responsibility is always 重い責任, never 強い or 高い.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]には、{軽[かる]い|cl-adj}かばんを持[も]って行[い]きます。
en: I take a light bag on trips.
why: A bag with little weight is 軽い; 重い/軽い is the pair for weight.

jp: 朝[あさ]は胃[い]が疲[つか]れているので、{薄[うす]い|cl-adj}お茶[ちゃ]がいいです。
en: My stomach is tired in the morning, so weak tea is better.
why: Tea of little strength is 薄いお茶, the opposite of 濃いお茶.

jp: ラーメンのスープが{濃[こ]かった|cl-adj}ので、あとで水[みず]が飲[の]みたくなりました。
en: The ramen soup was strongly flavored, so afterwards I wanted water.
why: Strongly seasoned soup is 濃い; 濃い/薄い is the pair for the taste of soup.

jp: 山[やま]の上[うえ]は風[かぜ]が{強[つよ]くて|cl-adj}、帽子[ぼうし]が飛[と]んでしまいました。
en: The wind was strong at the top of the mountain and my hat blew away.
why: Wind that blows a hat away is 風が強い.

jp: 風[かぜ]が{弱[よわ]い|cl-adj}日[ひ]は、洗濯物[せんたくもの]がなかなか乾[かわ]きません。
en: On days when the wind is weak, the laundry doesn't dry easily.
why: A day with little wind is 風が弱い; 強い/弱い pairs with 風.

jp: 兄[あに]は少[すこ]し飲[の]んだだけで寝[ね]てしまうほど、お酒[さけ]が{弱[よわ]い|cl-adj}です。
en: My older brother is so weak with alcohol that he falls asleep after only a little.
why: Little tolerance for alcohol is お酒が弱い, not 軽い or 低い.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]はお酒[さけ]が{強[つよ]くて|cl-adj}、飲[の]み会[かい]ではいつも最後[さいご]まで元気[げんき]です。
en: She can hold her liquor, so she is always lively until the end of drinking parties.
why: Being resistant to alcohol is お酒が強い, the opposite of 弱い.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]を引[ひ]いて、夜[よる]に熱[ねつ]が{高[たか]く|cl-adj}なりました。
en: I caught a cold and my fever went up at night.
why: A rising fever is 熱が高くなる; temperature is high or low.

jp: 薬[くすり]を飲[の]んだので、今日[きょう]は熱[ねつ]が昨日[きのう]より{低[ひく]い|cl-adj}です。
en: I took medicine, so my fever is lower today than yesterday.
why: A fever is compared as high or low, so a lower fever is 熱が低い, the opposite of 熱が高い.

jp: 午後[ごご]は{激[はげ]しい|cl-adj}雨[あめ]になるので、早[はや]めに帰[かえ]りましょう。
en: It will turn into heavy rain in the afternoon, so let's go home early.
why: Heavy downpours are 激しい雨; the other adjectives do not describe rain.

jp: 塩[しお]を入[い]れすぎて、スープの味[あじ]が{濃[こ]く|cl-adj}なってしまいました。
en: I put in too much salt and the soup became too strongly flavored.
why: Too much salt makes the taste 濃い; 薄く would be the result of adding water.

jp: 水[みず]を足[た]したら、味[あじ]が{薄[うす]く|cl-adj}なりました。
en: When I added water, the flavor became weak.
why: Diluting with water makes the taste 薄い, the opposite of 濃い.
